angle: Treat AI like long-dated infrastructure: unit economics guardrails beat hype and lock-in.
sourceTitle: The Hidden Financial Risks of the AI Boom
linkedinPost:
AI budgets rarely blow up on day one—they decay into unsustainable run rates.

Knowledge at Wharton flags the financing risks behind the AI boom. I see the enterprise version daily: multi-year commitments, vendor lock-in, and usage that drifts away from value while the invoice compounds.

My take: treat AI like long-dated infrastructure with strict unit economics.

- Define the unit. $ per successful outcome (resolved ticket, qualified lead, prevented fraud), not $ per token or seat.
- Set guardrails. Hard kill-switches when $/outcome crosses a threshold or quality dips.
- Stage commitments. Step-up capacity only after proving unit economics at each tier.
- Hedge dependency. Contractual exit ramps and data/weights portability where possible.

Finance and product need a shared dashboard: usage, quality, and cost per outcome on one page. If you can’t show payback period and sensitivity to rate changes, you’re financing hope.

What’s the one metric you’d tie to every AI invoice next quarter? #AIStrategy #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI
xPost: Don’t finance hope. Tie AI spend to $/successful outcome, add kill-switches when it drifts, and stage commitments only after unit economics are proven. Treat AI like long-dated infrastructure, not a blank check. #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI
